text:
Predicates:
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
In(x, y) ::: city x is in state y.
SameState(x, y) ::: city x and city y are in the same state.
Exception(x) ::: x is an exception city that can be in more than one state.

Premises:
City(billings) ∧ In(billings, montana) ::: Billings is a city in the state of Montana in U.S.
City(butte) ∧ City(helena) ∧ City(missoula) ∧ In(butte, montana) ∧ In(helena, montana) ∧ In(missoula, montana) ::: The state of Montana includes the cities of Butte, Helena, and Missoula.
City(whiteSulphurSprings) ∧ City(butte) ∧ SameState(whiteSulphurSprings, butte) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in the same state in U.S.
City(stPierre) ∧ ¬In(stPierre, montana) ::: The city of St Pierre is not in the state of Montana.
∀x (In(x, butte) → ¬In(x, stPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((City(x) ∧ State(y) ∧ State(z) ∧ In(x, y) ∧ In(x, z)) → (x = bristol ∨ x = texarkana ∨ x = texhoma ∨ x = unionCity)) ::: A city can only be in one state in U.S. except for Bristol, Texarkana, Texhoma and Union City.

Conclusion:
¬SameState(butte, stPierre) ::: Butte and St Pierre are not in the same state.
